senses.def: the second son of Adam and Eve and the brother of Cain
the state of remaining awake because of not being able to go to sleep, whether from anxiety or because of external circumstances
senses.comment: In the two occurrences of ἀγρυπνία in the NT (2 Corinthians 6:5), failure to sleep was evidently the result of external circumstances which prevented normal sleep. It may therefore be possible to translate ἀγρυπνία as it was not possible to sleep or there was no way to sleep.

senses.def: to speak of the excellence of a person, object, or event
senses.comment: In a number of languages praise can only be expressed by direct discourse, and this requires some content which provides the basis for praise. For example, in Luke 2:13 instead of a literal rendering of ‘praising God,’ it may be necessary to have ‘they said, God is wonderful,’ and in Luke 16:8 it may be necessary to translate ‘the master of this dishonest manager said, You are remarkable for having done such a clever thing.’

senses.def: (derivative of ἀκροάομαι ‘to hear,’ not occurring in the NT) one who hears
senses.comment: In rendering Romans 2:13, it may be necessary to specify certain limitations with regard to being ‘hearers,’ for example, ‘for not just those who listen to the Law are righteous in God’s sight’ or ‘for those who merely listen to the Law are not the ones who are righteous in God’s sight.’

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to act contrary to the will and law of God
to accept the presence of a person with friendliness
to experience something as the recipient of an event
to cause to die on a cross a second time
senses.comment: In extrabiblical Greek ἀνασταυρόω is essentially equivalent in meaning to σταυρόω (20.76), but in Hebrews 6:6 ἀνασταυρόω is used figuratively of believers whose sin causes Christ to be crucified again in the sense of exposing Christ to public shame by virtue of the misdeeds of his professed followers. Some scholars, however, interpret ἀνασταυρόω in Hebrews 6:6 as referring simply to the original crucifixion and thus interpret ἀνασταυρόω as being essentially synonymous with σταυρόω.

senses.def: pertaining to unwillingness to use one’s mental faculties in order to understand
senses.comment: As in the case of ἀσύνετος (32.49), the meaning of ἀνόητος is that people presumably would not use their capacity for understanding and as a result, thought and behaved foolishly. ἀνόητος does not imply the mental state of being an idiot or imbecile.

senses.def: to announce or inform, with possible focus upon the source of information
to announce what must be done
senses.comment: This meaning is found as a variant reading only: ὁ θεὸς, τὰ νῦν ἀπαγγέλλει τοῖς ἀνθρώποις πάντας πανταχοῦ μετανοεῖν ‘now God orders all people everywhere to turn away from their evil ways’ Acts 17:30 (apparatus).

senses.def: to give a tenth of one’s income
to cause someone to pay a tenth
senses.comment: In a number of languages there are problems involved in speaking of ‘a tenth,’ and accordingly there are difficulties in formulating expressions about ‘tithing.’ In some languages one may speak of ‘a tenth’ as ‘one part of ten parts’ or ‘one part together with nine parts.’ ‘To tithe’ may be rendered as ‘from ten parts to pay one part’ or ‘to pay one part and to keep nine parts.’

senses.def: one who fulfills the role of being a special messenger (generally restricted to the immediate followers of Jesus Christ, but also extended, as in the case of Paul, to other early Christians active in proclaiming the message of the gospel)
senses.comment: The relationship of an apostle to Jesus Christ is sometimes expressed as ‘being Christ’s messenger’ or ‘being a special messenger of Jesus Christ.’ In such a phrase, the term ‘special’ refers to having been commissioned by Jesus Christ for a particular task or role.

senses.def: (derivative of ἀποστέλλω[b] ‘to send a message,’ 15.67) one who is sent with a message

large wild four-footed mammal with thick fur and doglike face; walks on all fours but may stand up on its back legs to get a better view; may be 2 m. tall when standing up and weigh over 200 kilos; feeds on roots, berries, wild fruit, mice, and lizards, and, occasionally, small livestock; Ursus arctos syriacus; dangerous when provoked or robbed of cubs; associated with violence and danger
senses.comment: The term ἄρκος ‘bear’ occurs in the NT only in Revelation 13:2 as a description of the apocalyptic beast. In languages where a term for bear is not known, it is probably best to borrow a word and describe the referent in a footnote or glossary. In Revelation 13:2 a somewhat descriptive phrase is sometimes employed, for example, ‘with large feet having claws like those of an animal called bear.’ By this means the information about the bear’s feet has been incorporated into the text, but usually it is better to leave such information to a marginal note.

senses.def: to engage in some activity, with both continuity and effort
pertaining to being happy or content with what one has
glosses: content with the circumstances in which one exists

senses.def: a sorcerer and prophet summoned by Balak to curse Israel
a village on the Mount of Olives
a place on the east side of the Jordan where John baptized
(a figurative extension of meaning of βραχίων ‘arm,’ not occurring in the NT) power as an expression of the activity of a person or supernatural being
senses.comment: In some languages there is no abstract term for ‘power.’ The equivalent of doing something by the power of someone is ‘someone makes it possible to do’ or, in a figurative sense, ‘someone gives strength to do.’

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: exalted arm, or: lifted up arm) great power, with the implication of an exalted quality
a fertile plain south of Capernaum
a name for the Lake of Galilee, also called the Lake of Tiberias

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.def: the watery fluid which flows from the eye
the psychological faculty of understanding, reasoning, thinking, and deciding
senses.comment: In some languages there is no noun such as English mind, and therefore one must use a verb expression meaning ‘to think,’ ‘to reason,’ or ‘to understand,’ depending upon the particular context. In some languages the closest equivalent of ‘mind’ may be a figurative extension of a term meaning ‘head,’ but more often than not, thinking is regarded as being in some other part of the body, for example, ‘heart’ or ‘liver.’

senses.def: a particular manner or way of thinking
senses.comment: In a number of languages it may be necessary to render ‘way of thinking’ by a clause, for example, ‘how people think.’ In the case of 1 Peter 4:1, it may be necessary to translate ‘you too must strengthen yourselves by thinking just like Christ thought.’

senses.def: the content of thinking and reasoning
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is simply not possible to find noun-like words for thinking or reasoning and therefore it may be necessary to use a verb equivalent throughout. For example, in Luke 11:17 one may translate as ‘but Jesus knew what they were thinking.’

senses.def: to provide detailed information in a systematic manner
to give an object, usually implying value
(derivative of δίδωμι[a] ‘to give,’ 57.71) that which is given
a Jewish festival commemorating the rededication of the Temple in the time of Judas Maccabaeus in 165 B.C.
glosses: the festival of dedication of the Temple
senses.comment: It may be possible to speak of this Festival of Dedication as ‘the festival to celebrate the time when the Temple was again made pure and ready for worship.’

senses.def: to run or rush quickly in to
to change to a state of control over one’s thought processes
glosses: to come to one’s right senses
to change to a proper state of mind
senses.comment: The equivalent of ‘to come to one’s senses’ may be in some languages ‘to think again as one should think’ or ‘to no longer have crazy ideas.’

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to show kindness or concern for someone in serious need
(a figurative extension of meaning of ἔμφυτος ‘to be implanted,’ not occurring in the NT) to be permanently in a place, with the implication of development
to speak to someone on behalf of someone else

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to despise someone or something on the basis that it is worthless or of no value

senses.subdomain: On, Upon, On the Surface Of
senses.def: a position on a surface of an object, whether vertical or horizontal, and in contact with the object
a position in proximity to or in the immediate vicinity of an object or other position
a position within an area determined by other objects and distributed among such objects

senses.subdomain: In Front Of, Face To Face, In Back Of, Behind
senses.def: a position before, with the implication of a relationship of authority
extension toward a goal, usually implying reaching the goal
extension to a goal, with implied contact on a horizontal surface
(with the accusative) a marker of the one upon whom responsibility falls
senses.comment: See also 37.102.

senses.def: a marker of the experiencer, often with the implication of an action by a superior force or agency
(with the dative) a marker of instrument as the basis for some event
(with the accusative or dative) a marker of opposition in a judicial or quasijudicial context
(with the dative) a marker of persons benefited by an event, with the implication of their being in a dependent relationship
a marker of an addition to what already exists, but with the possible implication of something more significant
a marker of the object over which someone exercises a control or authority
a marker of cause or reason as the basis for a subsequent event or state
a marker of purpose, pointing to the goal of an event or state
(with the genitive) a marker of content as a means of specifying a particular referent
a marker of the basis of some event

senses.subdomain: Up To, As Much As, To the Degree That [Marked Extent of Degree]
senses.def: a degree extending to a particular point as marked by the context
senses.comment: See also Romans 11:13 in 78.52.

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
senses.def: a marker of a point of time which is simultaneous to or overlaps with another point of time

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time with Reference to Some Unit of Time: During, In, While, Throughout
senses.def: a marker of the extent of time within a unit

senses.subdomain: Agent, Personal or Nonpersonal, Causative or Immediate, Direct or Indirect
senses.def: (with the accusative) a marker of agent, with the added implication of effect upon the agent
senses.comment: It is possible that in 2 Thessalonians 1:10 there is a double relation marked by ἐπί, for it may be construed as marking the affected participant with τὸ μαρτύριον and at the same time the agent participant with ἐπιστεύθη. It is this double role which may account for the use of ἐπί rather than ὑπό, which would clearly mark a relation with ἐπιστεύθη, or πρός, which would indicate clearly a relation with μαρτύριον.

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: at the doors) a point of time subsequent to another point of time and indicating imminence, that is to say, the subsequent event is regarded as almost begun

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
senses.def: pertaining to a relatively long duration of time

senses.subdomain: Assign to a Role or Function
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: upon someone’s head) to accept responsibility for some action, often with the implication of blame
senses.comment: This statement in Acts 18:6 is no doubt an adage meaning that anything bad which may happen to a person, including one’s death, will be one’s own responsibility, and therefore no one else is to blame.|It is also possible to classify this idiom in Domain 90D. Note that in 37.102 the focus is on the assignment of responsibility.

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to sit upon the seat of Moses) to have the capacity to interpret the Law of Moses with authority
glosses: to be an authority concerning the Law of Moses

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: on the housetops) pertaining to being widely known in view of the events in question having taken place in public

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: upon enough) duration of time for a considerable period, with the focus upon sufficiency of time
glosses: during a considerable period of time

senses.def: to long for something, with the implication of recognizing a lack
a companion of Paul
a city treasurer

senses.subdomain: Acceptable To, To Be Pleased With
senses.def: that which pleases someone
(derivative of εὐδοκέω[c] ‘to prefer,’ 30.97) that which is desired on the basis of its appearing to be beneficial
expressing gratitude for benefits or blessings
senses.comment: Thanks is often expressed in highly idiomatic ways. For example, in some languages one says thank you by saying ‘may God pay you.’ Such a phrase may be so standardized as to even be used in expressing thankfulness to God himself. In other instances, thankfulness may be expressed as ‘you have made my heart warm.’

senses.def: pertaining to experiencing happiness, based primarily upon the pleasure derived
pertaining to having the nature of God
(derivative of θεός[a] ‘God,’ 12.1) the nature or state of being God
senses.comment: The expression ‘divine nature’ may be rendered in a number of languages as ‘just what God is like’ or ‘how God is’ or ‘what God is.’ In Romans 1:20 ‘deity’ may sometimes be expressed as ‘the fact that he is God’ or ‘… is truly God.’|In 2 Peter 1:4 ‘to share in the very being of God,’ one may speak of ‘to share in what God is like’ or ‘to become in a measure like God.’ It is important, of course, to avoid the implication that people can become completely God.

senses.def: pertaining to being made or consisting of citron wood (that is, from a citron tree, a coniferous tree related to cypresses, pines, and cedars; up to 9 m high; scaly leaves, reddish brown bark, sweet-smelling wood)
senses.comment: The citron tree belongs to the citrus family of plants, and it produces a pale yellow fruit somewhat larger than a lemon, the rind of which is often candied. In Revelation 18:12, however, the focus is upon the fine quality of the wood, and since citron trees are not known in many parts of the world, it may be useful to translate πᾶν ξύλον θύϊνον simply as ‘all kinds of valuable wood.’

senses.def: the means by which sins are forgiven
senses.comment: Though some traditional translations render ἱλαστήριον as ‘propitiation,’ this involves a wrong interpretation of the term in question. Propitiation is essentially a process by which one does a favor to a person in order to make him or her favorably disposed, but in the NT God is never the object of propitiation since he is already on the side of people. ἱλασμός and ἱλαστήριον[a] denote the means of forgiveness and not propitiation.

senses.def: the location or place where sins are forgiven (in traditional translations rendered mercy seat)
a king of Judah mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to being bad, with the implication of harmful and damaging
senses.comment: The implication in Acts 23:5 is that one must not speak in such a way as ‘to cause harm to.’

senses.def: pertaining to having experienced harm
senses.comment: The phrase κακῶς πάσχει in Matthew 17:15 may be a reference to a type of epileptic seizure.

senses.def: pertaining to being incorrect or inaccurate, with the possible implication of also being reprehensible
a high point on a scale of extent and implying harm and seriousness of the state
(an idiom, literally: to have badly, or: to fare badly) to be in a bad state, to be ill (to some extent equivalent to the English idiom ‘to be bad off,’ in speaking of ill health)
to wear a covering over one’s head
(derivative of κατασκοπέω to observe secretly, 24.50) one whose task it is to obtain information surreptitiously
a city on the Lake of Galilee
to cause something to be shut
senses.comment: In some languages the equivalent of this expression in Acts 5:23 would be ‘we found the jail securely locked.’

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to close the bowels) to refuse to show compassion
to engage in hard work, implying difficulties and trouble
to be tired or weary, as the result of hard or difficult endeavor
senses.comment: It is also possible to interpret κοπιάω in Matthew 11:28 as κοπιάω[a] ‘to work hard’ (see 42.47).

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of κοπιάω[b] ‘to be tired,’ 23.78) to become emotionally fatigued and discouraged
a larger type of domesticated animal, primarily one used for riding or carrying loads
senses.comment: In 1 Corinthians 15:39 (ἄλλη δὲ σὰρξ κτηνῶν, ἄλλη δὲ σὰρξ πτηνῶν, ἄλλη δὲ ἰχθύων ‘another is the flesh of animals, another the flesh of birds, and another the flesh of fish’) one might argue that κτηνῶν is simply a highly generic expression for all kinds of animals, but in view of its meaning in so many other contexts, it probably applies even in 1 Corinthians 15:39 to large domesticated animals.|As in so many instances, the translator must render passages in terms of expressions which are appropriate to particular contexts. For example, in Acts 23:24 a translation such as ‘horses’ would be appropriate, while in Luke 10:34 the term ‘donkey’ would be fitting, and in Revelation 18:13 κτήνη (in which κτῆνος contrasts with πρόβατα ‘sheep’) would perhaps best be translated as ‘cattle.’

senses.def: a city on the south coast of the island of Crete
to speak in a highly insulting manner

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
senses.def: pertaining to a relatively long duration of time
pertaining to being far from some point of reference
to keep on giving serious consideration to something
glosses: to let one’s mind dwell on
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand μελετάω in 1 Timothy 4:15 as meaning ‘to do’ or ‘to practice,’ as noted in 68.20.

senses.subdomain: To Intend, To Purpose, To Plan
senses.def: to think seriously about a particular course of action
to continue to perform certain activities with care and concern
senses.comment: The construction in 1 Timothy 4:15, in which ταῦτα μελέτα and ἐν τούτοις ἴσθι appear to be essentially synonymous reinforcements one of the other, would appear to fully justify combining these expressions as essentially equivalent in meaning, but for another interpretation of μελετάω in 1 Timothy 4:15, see 30.20.

senses.def: one who shares with someone else as an associate in an enterprise or undertaking

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: sexual intercourse of a man with a married woman other than his own spouse
senses.comment: From the standpoint of the NT, adultery was normally defined in terms of the married status of the woman involved in any such act. In other words, sexual intercourse of a married man with an unmarried woman would usually be regarded as πορνεία ‘fornication’ (88.271), but sexual intercourse of either an unmarried or a married man with someone else’s wife was regarded as adultery, both on the part of the man as well as the woman. In view of the married status of the woman being the determining factor in μοιχάω, μοιχεύω, μοιχάομαι, μοιχεία, and related terms (88.277-88.278), there is a significant contrast with πορνεύω and related expressions (88.271). πορνεύω, however, may be regarded as more generic in meaning, and thus in certain contexts including adultery.|Matthew 5:32 is usually rendered as ‘anyone who divorces his wife for any cause other than fornication makes her guilty of committing adultery,’ presumably on the implication that she would marry someone else, as is implied in the final clause of the verse.

senses.def: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

senses.comment: In most languages east and west are related to the rising or setting sun, although in some languages there may be some local geographical feature which serves as a marker of direction, for example, the location of a particular mountain, the ocean, or a river. For north, some languages employ ‘to the left of the rising sun,’ that is to say, the direction is oriented in terms of the left hand of a person facing toward the rising sun. Similarly, south would be ‘to the right of the rising sun.’

senses.def: a wind which blows from the south
senses.comment: A number of languages have terms for winds coming from or going toward different directions. In a number of cases, however, directional expressions are not included in the terms for such winds. For example, a north wind may be simply called ‘a cold wind,’ and a south wind might be called ‘a wind from the sea.’ Such expressions depend upon local geographical features. Even in the instance in which a south wind is described in terms of direction, it may be necessary to use a somewhat expanded phrase, for example, ‘a wind from the right of the rising sun.’ Such an expression is based upon the experience of a person facing the rising sun and determining the south in terms of the right side of the person.

senses.def: a task involving management and organization

senses.subdomain: To Intend, To Purpose, To Plan
senses.def: a plan which involves a set of arrangements (referring in the NT to God’s plan for bringing salvation to mankind within the course of history)
to manage and provide for a household
glosses: to be in charge of a household
senses.comment: In biblical times a household would consist of more than the nuclear family, that is to say, more than simply husband, wife, and children, for servants, slaves, and permanent hired workers living with the family would be regarded as a part of the total household.

senses.def: a Christian mentioned in 2 Timothy 1:16 and 2 Timothy 4:19

senses.subdomain: Whom or What Spoken or Written About
senses.def: a reference to an indefinite entity, event, or state
senses.comment: Often translated as ‘who’, which, or what, since these pronouns in English are often indefinite in meaning.

senses.def: a female slave

senses.subdomain: Land in Contrast With the Sea
senses.def: a territory bordering on the sea, in contrast with an inland area (compare ἀνωτερικός, 1.65)
senses.comment: Frequently παράλιος must be translated by a phrase, for example, ‘the land along the seaside’ or ‘the countries bordering on the sea.’

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
senses.def: to mark the passage of time, with focus upon completion
a marker of something in addition to what is already implied in the context
to cause to happen, with the implication of fulfilling some purpose
to relate fully the content of a message
to fully accomplish one’s task
to be completely certain of the truth of something
to attack with the intent or result of destroying
to happen or occur previous to some point of time
to need or lack something further or in addition
glosses: to be in need of something more
senses.comment: One may also render Acts 17:25 as ‘there is nothing that he needs that people can supply by working for him.’

senses.def: to exist prior to some temporal reference point

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time without Reference to Other Points of Time: Time, Occasion, Ever, Often
senses.def: an indefinite point of time or occasion

senses.subdomain: Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
senses.def: (derivative of σάββατον[a], 67.184) a special religiously significant period for rest and worship

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to appropriate, befitting behavior and implying dignity and respect
pertaining to being crooked or winding

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of σκολιός[a] ‘crooked,’ 79.90) pertaining to being unscrupulous and dishonest
(derivative of στάσις[a] ‘insurrection,’ 39.34) a person who engages in insurrection
permission to do something (implying some type of concession)
to take along with, with emphasis upon accompaniment
to engage in an activity together with someone else
the son of Hamor (τοῦ Συχέμ, apparatus)
a city in Samaria

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
senses.def: a very brief period of time
glosses: quickly (in combination with the preposition ἐν)
senses.comment: In Acts 22:18 τάχος evidently refers to a brief period of time before fulfilling the admonition to leave Jerusalem.

senses.def: to experience something bad, often in retribution for some wrongdoing

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to live a life of luxury, usually associated with intemperate feasting and drinking
glosses: to live a life of luxury

senses.def: to engage in an activity beyond some implied limit, whether in intensity or extent
senses.comment: There are significant differences of opinion with regard to the interpretation of 2 Corinthians 10:14, and these differences should no doubt be reflected in marginal notes.

senses.def: a female pig (χοῖρος)

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to friendly concern and kindness toward someone
to keep on giving serious consideration to something
glosses: to let one’s mind dwell on

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.def: a hand or any relevant portion of the hand, including, for example, the fingers
senses.comment: In rendering Matthew 8:3 it would be inappropriate in some languages to translate literally ‘he stretched out his hand,’ since this would imply some kind of miracle of extending the hand itself. A correct rendering may be ‘he extended his arm and touched him with his hand.’|In Luke 15:22 χείρ refers to the finger, not to the hand, and therefore it is necessary to translate in most languages ‘put a ring on his finger.’

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of χείρ[a] ‘hand,’ 8.30) a human as an agent in some activity
(a figurative extension of meaning of χείρ[a] ‘hand,’ 8.30) power as an expression of the activity of a person or supernatural being
senses.comment: In some languages there is no abstract term for ‘power.’ The equivalent of doing something by the power of someone is ‘someone makes it possible to do’ or, in a figurative sense, ‘someone gives strength to do.’

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of χείρ[a] ‘hand,’ 8.30) a state of control exercised by a person
glosses: to be in the control of
to be in the power of
senses.comment: In some languages it may be necessary to express the meaning of ‘control’ in the context of Acts 12:11 by a more specific reference to potential action, for example, ‘he rescued me and Herod could not do anything to me.’

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to give into the hands) to hand someone over into the control of others
glosses: to deliver to the control of
senses.comment: In a context such as Matthew 26:45, παραδίδοται εἰς χεῖρας may be rendered as ‘will hand him over to be arrested’ or ‘will cause him to be taken into custody.’

senses.subdomain: Agent, Personal or Nonpersonal, Causative or Immediate, Direct or Indirect
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: with the hand of) a marker of an associated agent
(an idiom, literally: human hand) a human being as a means of accomplishing something
(an idiom, literally: to lay hands on) to take a person into custody for alleged illegal activity
(a Semitic idiom, literally: one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back) to begin some activity requiring close attention but then to change one’s mind about proceeding
glosses: to start to do something and then to hesitate
to begin but have second thoughts about continuing
senses.comment: It is probably best to regard the phrase ἐπιβαλὼν τὴν χεῖρα ἐπ᾽ ἄροτρον καὶ βλέπων εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω as a part of a traditional saying referring to anyone who has second thoughts about undertaking some new or different enterprise, but the particular manner in which this is adapted to a statement concerning ‘the kingdom of God’ makes its strictly idiomatic structure somewhat doubtful.

senses.def: (an idiom, literally to stretch out hands upon) to take a person into custody for alleged illegal activity
to move on from one place to another
senses.comment: In translating Matthew 15:17 it may be necessary to add an element which suggests swallowing, since something which enters a person’s mouth does not automatically go into the stomach. Accordingly, it may be necessary to translate ‘anything that goes into a person’s mouth and is swallowed goes on then into his stomach.’ It would also be possible to say ‘anything that goes into one’s throat goes on then into a person’s stomach.’|In John 8:37 χωρέω[a] appears to be used figuratively in the statement ὁ λόγος ὁ ἐμὸς οὐ χωρεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν ‘my word makes no progress in you,’ but it is also possible to interpret χωρέω in this context as referring to an adequate place, for example, ‘my word finds no room in you’ (see 80.4).

senses.def: to be a quantity of space
to be able to accept a message and respond accordingly
senses.comment: It is possible to understand χωρέω in Matthew 19:11 as meaning ‘to be able to understand.’

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of χωρέω[b] ‘to have room for,’ 80.4) to be friendly disposed toward someone
